This naive uniform-random constructor explains the plateau: uniform random points in a square include hull-interior clusters that produce tiny near-collinear triangles, and the configuration is never refined. I replace exactly those three lines with a self-contained, deterministic multi-seed + local-refinement Heilbronn constructor: it builds seven structurally distinct seeds (regular 13-gon, ellipse variant, two-cluster arcs, rounded-square superellipse, spiral+triangle anchors, perturbed polygon, seeded random), all constructed directly in the valid domain (hull scaled to unit area at construction time, no post-hoc fixup), evaluates the min normalized triangle area for each via an O(n³) vectorized cross-product computation, and applies a coordinate-descent local refinement (pairwise perturbations with shrinking step size, keeping a point only if it strictly improves the objective and stays within the unit-area hull) to the best seed. Everything uses the fixed seed and closed-form geometry, so results are deterministic and reproducible.
